newsitem.title: INDIA: India VSNL GDR attracts global investors.
newsitem.headline: India VSNL GDR attracts global investors.

text.p: Telecommunications firm Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd's (VSNL) successful jumbo issue of global depositary receipts (GDRs) received 642 orders from investors in 28 countries, a source close to the deal said on Tuesday.
VSNL's issue -- India's largest ever GDR offering and its first overseas equity issue this year -- was priced on Monday at $13.93 per GDR, or 1,000 rupees per local share.

On Tuesday, VSNL GDRs listed in London were trading above their issue price at $17.60/17.95, traders said. VSNL shares jumped 84.75 rupees, or 8.6 percent, to close at 1,070 on the Bombay Stock Exchange.
"The issue was ten times oversubscribed at all price levels," the source told Reuters. He said the book had been oversubscribed by around 2.5 to 3.0 times at 1,000 rupees.
VSNL raised $526.5 million through its long-awaited GDR, previously twice delayed, making it the third largest international equity offering from Asia, excluding Japan.
Investment banking sources said U.S. institutional investors bought 33 percent of the issue. Funds in Britain picked up 30 percent of the issue with Asia contributing another 22 percent, they said.
The remaining 15 percent of the investment came from other parts of Europe and the Middle East.

"There was some interest from a number of countries that are not traditionally associated with investing in India like Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Portugal and New Zealand," the source said. "A number of new countries cropped up."
Investment bankers said the proceeds from the issue would be kept in dollars, and were unlikely to hit the local market.
Some foreign exchange dealers said earlier on Tuesday the GDR proceeds could enter the local market at a time when the Indian market is awash with dollars.
"It's quite clear that the proceeds are going to remain in dollars," the source said, adding that the company was unlikely to bring the money into the country this month.

"We are delighted with the success of the VSNL GDR issue. The demand from international investors has been outstanding and reflects VSNL's position as a global telecom service provider," VSNL chairman and managing director Brijendra Syngal said in a statement after the pricing.
Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, Jardine Fleming and Salomon Brothers were global coordinators to the GDR issue.
VSNL plans to offer 600,000 shares to domestic retail investors later in the year.
